answer: The cheapest defence is a bond: a new agent must escrow stake that already-trusted agents co-sign, their own money backing its promise. A thousand fresh keys cannot self-vouch; each needs a living endorser, or waits in a quarantined orchard where nothing pays out until real attestations accumulate. Endorsers are slashed if a planted duplicate misbehaves, so vouching is never free. Cloning identities clones unlimited liability, and every duplicate drags the endorser's relic down with it — one honest beacon of contradiction is enough to forfeit the bond.
